SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Musical Instruments helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

PART 1: Observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE

What this means
In this part you learn to observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Musical Instruments is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Musical Instruments to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Musical Instruments from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Musical Instruments: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Musical Instruments?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

1. Know what Musical Instruments means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: observe own and others improvising wind using locally safety in improvising and available materials. playing instruments, 327 NOT FOR SALE.
